    How it works

    1. Upload a file, up to 50 GB. No account.
    2. Share the link right away. It works as soon as the upload is done.
    3. It’s deleted when the link expires, after one download, or when you delete it.

    Use fyl in your terminal

    One command uploads a file and prints its link. No account, and nothing is stored on your computer.

    bash — fyl

    # install or update

    $curl -fsSL https://fyl.at/cli/install | sh

    Installed fyl to /usr/local/bin

    # then send a file

    $fyl ./archive.zip

    https://fyl.at/d/…

    For macOS and Linux; needs only curl. The installer checks fyl against its published checksum and puts it in /usr/local/bin, so it may ask for your password. Run it again to update.

    # with the settings on this page

    $fyl ./archive.zip

    https://fyl.at/d/…

    # other lifetimes, or a single download

    $fyl ./archive.zip --expires 3d
    $fyl ./secret.txt --expires 1h --once

    Links last 1 day unless you choose 5m to 7d. fyl prints only the link, so url="$(fyl ./archive.zip)" works in scripts. --password asks for a password, or makes one up if you just press Enter. If an upload breaks off, fyl prints a --resume command that continues it within 24 hours.

    # download with the original filename

    $curl -fOJ 'https://fyl.at/d/<id>/archive.zip'

    # a link with a password: curl asks for it

    $curl -fOJ -u fyl 'https://fyl.at/d/<id>'

    # an encrypted link: fyl decrypts it, and asks for the key if the link has none

    $fyl download 'https://fyl.at/d/<id>#<key>'

    Paste the link you received. A one-time link can be resumed from the same network until the download finishes.

    # keep the management link

    $fyl ./archive.zip --manage

    https://fyl.at/d/… https://fyl.at/#manage/…

    # delete it before it expires

    $fyl rm 'https://fyl.at/#manage/<id>/<key>'

    Deleted archive.zip.

    --manage adds the private management link as a second line. Keep it safe: it is the only way to delete the file or change its expiry, and anyone who has it can do both.
